variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: Model evaluation is the process of measuring whether an ML model generalizes to unseen data and produces acceptable outcomes under production conditions. Testing extends beyond model accuracy to data contracts, latency, reliability, fairness, and business impact.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “How should the task determine the evaluation strategy?”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Classification
pairs.detail: Use precision, recall, calibration, and cost-weighted errors when classes or consequences are imbalanced.
pairs.explanation: Use precision, recall, calibration, and cost-weighted errors when classes or consequences are imbalanced. Split by the unit that could leak across examples.

pairs.label: Regression
pairs.detail: Use MAE or RMSE with residual slices and prediction intervals.
pairs.explanation: Use MAE or RMSE with residual slices and prediction intervals. Check outliers, heteroscedasticity, and whether large errors are concentrated in high-cost cases.

pairs.label: Time series
pairs.explanation: Backtest on forward-moving windows. Fit every transformation on the past only, and report quality across seasons and forecast horizons.

pairs.label: Ranking
pairs.detail: Use NDCG, MAP, or MRR within each query or request group.
pairs.explanation: Use NDCG, MAP, or MRR within each query or request group. Correct for position and exposure bias before treating clicks as relevance labels.

pairs.label: Generated output
pairs.detail: Combine task success, factuality, safety, style, and human review.
pairs.explanation: Combine task success, factuality, safety, style, and human review. Automated similarity metrics rarely establish usefulness alone.

pairs.label: All tasks
pairs.detail: Add latency, reliability, fairness, privacy, and business constraints that can block promotion even when the primary quality score improves.
pairs.explanation: Add latency, reliability, fairness, privacy, and business constraints that can block promotion even when the primary quality score improves.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. Use the full lesson’s worked examples and interactive labs to explore the trade-offs behind these questions.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Classification: Use precision, recall, calibration, and cost-weighted errors when classes or consequences are imbalanced. Regression: Use MAE or RMSE with residual slices and prediction intervals. Time series: Backtest on forward-moving windows. Ranking: Use NDCG, MAP, or MRR within each query or request group. Generated output: Combine task success, factuality, safety, style, and human review. All tasks: Add latency, reliability, fairness, privacy, and business constraints that can block promotion even when the primary quality score improves.

variants.prompt: From the lesson section “How does evidence promote a model safely?”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Lock the evaluation contract
pairs.detail: Name the population, split unit, primary metric, guardrails, minimum detectable effect, and failure slices before comparing candidates.
pairs.explanation: Name the population, split unit, primary metric, guardrails, minimum detectable effect, and failure slices before comparing candidates.

pairs.label: Test offline behavior
pairs.detail: Measure holdout quality, uncertainty, invariants, robustness, and latency against the current production baseline.
pairs.explanation: Measure holdout quality, uncertainty, invariants, robustness, and latency against the current production baseline.

pairs.label: Observe without authority
pairs.detail: Run the candidate on production inputs without changing user outcomes.
pairs.explanation: Run the candidate on production inputs without changing user outcomes. Verify feature compatibility, stability, and cost.

pairs.label: Limit real exposure
pairs.detail: Send a small, representative traffic slice to the candidate with automatic rollback conditions and comparable outcome logging.
pairs.explanation: Send a small, representative traffic slice to the candidate with automatic rollback conditions and comparable outcome logging.

pairs.label: Decide and keep watching
pairs.detail: Promote only when quality and guardrails pass, then retain the same cohort and slice checks for post-launch regression detection.
pairs.explanation: Promote only when quality and guardrails pass, then retain the same cohort and slice checks for post-launch regression detection.

variants.prompt: Aggregate quality improves by 4%, but a critical user slice regresses by 3% beyond its guardrail. What should the promotion gate do?
options: Hold or roll back while the slice regression is investigated
Promote because the aggregate score is larger
Delete the slice metric
Increase traffic to make the regression disappear
variants.explanation: A predeclared guardrail is a blocking contract. Aggregate quality cannot cancel a critical-slice regression.
